title: A Race Against Time
paragraphs: Life on Earth depends on a natural greenhouse effect: certain gases in the atmosphere absorb heat and slow its escape into space. Without it, the planet would be far too cold for most living things. The problem is not the effect itself but its strength, which has been growing as the concentration of these gases rises.

Carbon dioxide is the best known of them. It is released naturally by volcanoes and living organisms, but human activities now add far more, mainly through burning fossil fuels and clearing forests. According to NASA, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has risen by nearly fifty percent since seventeen fifty. Scientists can check this trend because tiny bubbles of ancient air are trapped in ice cores drilled from Greenland and Antarctica.

Those records show that the climate has always responded to changes in greenhouse gases. What is different today is the speed: NASA reports that the carbon dioxide added by people is increasing far faster than natural sources did after the last ice age. For that reason, reducing emissions is often described as a race against time.

sources.claim: Sera etkisi doğaldır: bazı gazlar ısıyı emip uzaya kaçışını yavaşlatır; karbondioksit volkanlar gibi doğal kaynaklardan ve fosil yakıt yakma ile ormansızlaşmadan gelir.
Atmosferdeki karbondioksit miktarı 1750'den beri neredeyse yüzde 50 arttı; insan kaynaklı karbondioksit, son buz çağından sonra doğal kaynakların artışından çok daha hızlı artıyor.
Grönland, Antarktika ve tropik buzullardan alınan buz çekirdekleri iklimin sera gazı seviyelerindeki değişimlere tepki verdiğini gösterir.
